title: The Fox and the Crow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Crow was sitting on a branch of a tree with a piece of cheese in her beak when a Fox observed her and set his wits to work to discover some way of getting the cheese. Coming and standing under the tree he looked up and said, "What a noble bird I see above me! Her beauty is without equal, the hue of her plumage exquisite. If only her voice is as sweet as her looks are fair, she ought without doubt to be Queen of the Birds." The Crow was hugely flattered by this, and just to show the Fox that she could sing she gave a loud caw. Down came the cheese, of course, and the Fox, snatching it up, said, "You have a voice, madam, I see: what you want is wits."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Crow holding in her beak?
options: A twig for her nest
A shiny coin
A piece of cheese
A small fish

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Crow sitting when the Fox first saw her?
options: On a branch of a tree
On top of a fence post
Beside a stream
On a stone wall

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say the Crow ought to be, if her voice is as sweet as her looks?
options: The fastest bird alive
A friend to every fox
The wisest bird in the forest
Queen of the Birds

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crow do to show the Fox that she could sing?
options: She flew down to the ground
She gave a loud caw
She hopped along the branch
She dropped the cheese at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the cheese the moment the Crow caws?
options: The Crow swallows it quickly
It rolls into a nearby stream
Down it comes, and the Fox snatches it up
The Fox climbs the tree to reach it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say to the Crow after he picks up the cheese?
options: "You have a voice, madam, I see: what you want is wits."
"Thank you for such a fine meal."
"I am sorry to have troubled you."
"Sing again, and I will return it."

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox praise the Crow's beauty and voice?
options: Because he truly admires how she sings
To distract her while another fox climbs the tree
Because he wants her to teach him to fly
To flatter her into singing so she drops the cheese

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's closing remark suggest about the Crow?
options: She is a better singer than the Fox expected
She has a fine voice but lacked the sense to see through flattery
She deliberately gave up the cheese out of kindness
She did not understand what the Fox had said to her

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Crow was "hugely flattered"?
options: She was deeply frightened by the Fox
She was confused by what the Fox said
She was greatly pleased by the praise
She was annoyed at being interrupted

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Flattery can trick even a proud listener into a costly mistake
Birds should never speak to foxes under any circumstances
A crow's voice is always more valuable than its meal
Foxes are unable to climb trees to reach their food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox call the Crow at the start of his praise?
options: A clever thief
A silent stranger
A tired traveller
A noble bird

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox praise about the Crow's appearance?
options: The size of her wings
The hue of her plumage
The color of her eyes
The shape of her beak

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Fox stand while he speaks to the Crow?
options: On a branch beside her
Beside a nearby stream
Under the tree
Behind a large rock

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Crow choose to caw so loudly for the Fox?
options: She wants to prove that her voice is as fine as her looks
She is warning the Fox to leave the tree
She is calling to other crows for help
She is trying to frighten the Fox away

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what lesson does the Crow's loss of the cheese suggest?
options: Singing loudly always frightens away hungry foxes
Cheese is too heavy for any bird to carry safely
Foxes never bother to speak to the birds they meet
Believing extravagant praise can cost you something valuable

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "snatching" describe about how the Fox takes the cheese?
options: Picking it up slowly and carefully
Grabbing it quickly and eagerly
Refusing to touch it at first
Sharing it evenly with the Crow

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A crow outwits a fox and keeps her cheese
Two foxes argue over which one saw the crow first
A fox flatters a vain crow and tricks her out of her cheese
A crow teaches a fox how to sing
